title: Nationwide Ground Stop: US Aviation Faces Major Tech Failure
subtitle: Millions of passengers face travel chaos after a rare system failure stops all flights across the United States.

summary.en: The Federal Aviation Administration issued a nationwide ground stop on Friday afternoon. This rare decision prevented all planes from taking off at airports across the country. Millions of passengers are currently stuck and waiting for updates. Officials are working to fix the technical problem as quickly as possible. The situation has caused significant travel disruption for travelers nationwide.
summary.zh: 聯邦航空總署於週五下午發布了全國性停飛令。這項罕見的決定禁止全國所有機場的飛機起飛。目前數百萬名旅客滯留並等待最新消息。官員正致力於儘速修復技術問題。此情況已對全國旅客造成嚴重的交通中斷。

paragraphs.en: On Friday afternoon, the United States aviation system faced a major challenge when the Federal Aviation Administration (FAA) issued a nationwide ground stop. This means that for a period of time, no airplanes were allowed to take off from any airport in the country. This is an extremely rare event that has left millions of passengers stuck at airports, unsure of when they will be able to reach their destinations.
paragraphs.zh: 週五下午，美國航空系統面臨重大挑戰，聯邦航空總署（FAA）發布了全國性的停飛令。這意味著在一段時間內，全國任何機場的飛機皆不得起飛。這是一起極為罕見的事件，導致數百萬名旅客滯留在機場，不確定何時才能抵達目的地。

paragraphs.en: According to NPR News, the FAA took this extraordinary step to ensure safety while they dealt with a serious technical failure. When the agency experiences problems with its computer systems, it cannot safely manage the flow of air traffic. By stopping all flights, the FAA prevents planes from being in the air without the necessary support from ground systems. This decision, while difficult for travelers, is designed to prevent accidents and keep the skies safe.
paragraphs.zh: 根據美國國家公共廣播電台（NPR）報導，聯邦航空總署採取這項非常手段，是為了在處理嚴重技術故障的同時確保安全。當該機構的電腦系統出現問題時，便無法安全地管理空中交通流量。透過暫停所有航班，聯邦航空總署防止了飛機在缺乏地面系統必要支援的情況下飛行。儘管這項決定對旅客造成困擾，但其目的是為了預防事故並維護天空的安全。

paragraphs.en: For many passengers, the news came as a surprise. Airports across the country quickly became crowded as travelers waited for information about their delayed or canceled flights. Many people were left waiting in long lines at ticket counters, hoping to rebook their travel or find out if their planes would eventually leave the ground. The scale of the disruption is massive, as the US aviation network is one of the busiest in the world, moving millions of people every single day.
paragraphs.zh: 對許多旅客而言，這則消息來得十分突然。隨著旅客等待關於航班延誤或取消的資訊，全國各地的機場迅速變得擁擠不堪。許多人被迫在櫃檯前排起長隊，希望能重新預訂行程，或確認他們的班機最終是否能夠起飛。此次中斷的規模相當龐大，因為美國航空網絡是全球最繁忙的網絡之一，每天運送數百萬名旅客。

paragraphs.en: Experts note that modern aviation relies heavily on complex computer systems to track flights, manage weather data, and communicate with pilots. When these systems fail, the entire network can stop working almost instantly. While the FAA has not yet provided full details on the exact cause of the failure, such events highlight how much the modern world depends on technology to function. Even a small error in a central system can lead to a nationwide problem that affects people in every state.
paragraphs.zh: 專家指出，現代航空高度依賴複雜的電腦系統來追蹤航班、管理氣象數據以及與機師溝通。當這些系統故障時，整個網絡幾乎會瞬間停止運作。雖然聯邦航空總署尚未提供關於故障確切原因的完整細節，但此類事件凸顯了現代世界對科技運作的依賴程度。即使是中央系統中的一個小錯誤，也可能引發影響全國各州民眾的問題。

paragraphs.en: Travelers are advised to check their flight status frequently and stay in contact with their airlines. Because the ground stop affects all airports, airlines are struggling to manage the sudden change in their schedules. Many flights that were already in the air were allowed to land, but no new flights were permitted to depart. This creates a "ripple effect," where a delay in one city causes delays in many other cities as planes and crews are unable to get to their next locations on time.
paragraphs.zh: 建議旅客頻繁查詢航班狀態，並與航空公司保持聯繫。由於停飛令影響所有機場，航空公司正努力應對時刻表突如其來的變動。許多已經在空中的航班獲准降落，但沒有新的航班被允許起飛。這產生了「漣漪效應」，即一個城市的延誤會導致許多其他城市的延誤，因為飛機和機組人員無法準時抵達下一個地點。

paragraphs.en: As the situation continues to develop, the focus remains on fixing the technical issue and getting the aviation system back to normal. The FAA is working around the clock to restore its services. However, even after the system is fixed, it will take time for the airlines to catch up and clear the backlog of passengers. Travelers should expect delays to last well beyond the initial ground stop as the industry works to return to its regular schedule.
paragraphs.zh: 隨著事態持續發展，焦點仍放在修復技術問題並讓航空系統恢復正常。聯邦航空總署正日以繼夜地恢復其服務。然而，即使系統修復後，航空公司仍需時間來追趕進度並消化滯留的旅客。旅客應預期延誤時間將遠超過最初的停飛期間，因為航空業正努力恢復正常時刻表。

paragraphs.en: This event serves as a reminder of the fragility of our transportation infrastructure. While flying is generally very safe, it requires perfect coordination between computers, air traffic controllers, and pilots. When that coordination is broken, the results are felt by millions of people at once. For now, the priority for the FAA and the airlines is safety, and they are asking for patience from the public as they work to resolve this difficult situation.
paragraphs.zh: 此事件提醒了我們交通基礎設施的脆弱性。雖然飛行通常非常安全，但它需要電腦、空中交通管制員與機師之間的完美協調。當這種協調中斷時，數百萬人會同時感受到影響。目前，聯邦航空總署與航空公司的首要任務是安全，他們也請求大眾在他們努力解決此困境時保持耐心。

keyTerms.definitionEn: An official order that prevents all aircraft from taking off from airports.
keyTerms.noteZh: 此詞組在航空領域有特定含義，指全面禁止起飛。文中：the Federal Aviation Administration (FAA) issued a nationwide ground stop.

keyTerms.definitionEn: A situation where one event causes a series of other events to happen one after another.
keyTerms.noteZh: 形容一個問題引發後續一連串的連鎖影響。文中：This creates a "ripple effect," where a delay in one city causes delays in many other cities as planes and crews are unable to get to their next locations on time.

keyTerms.definitionEn: To do the work or tasks that you should have done earlier because you were delayed.
keyTerms.noteZh: 這裡指航空公司在系統恢復後，處理先前累積的延誤。文中：it will take time for the airlines to catch up and clear the backlog of passengers.

keyTerms.definitionEn: A large amount of work or tasks that have not been finished and are waiting to be dealt with.
keyTerms.definitionZh: 積壓的工作或待處理事項
keyTerms.noteZh: 常見於商業或物流，指累積過多未處理的量。文中：it will take time for the airlines to catch up and clear the backlog of passengers.

quiz.question: What happened to the flights that were already in the air when the FAA issued the ground stop?

options.A: They were immediately diverted to the nearest international airport.
options.B: They were permitted to continue their journeys and land.
options.C: They were forced to return to their original departure airports.
options.D: They were grounded mid-flight by remote computer intervention.

quiz.explanationZh: 正確答案為 B。根據文章第五段，「Many flights that were already in the air were allowed to land」明確指出，已經在空中的班機被允許降落。選項 A 錯誤，因為文章未提及轉降國際機場；選項 C 錯誤，因為文章提到的是禁止起飛，而非要求返航；選項 D 錯誤，因為這在技術上不可行且文章未提及。

quiz.question: Why will the impact of the ground stop continue even after the technical failure is fixed?

options.A: Because the FAA needs to manually inspect every airplane before it can fly again.
options.B: Because the computer systems will require a nationwide software update.
options.C: Because the delay creates a chain reaction affecting crew and aircraft availability.
options.D: Because airports are legally required to keep terminals closed for 24 hours after a failure.

quiz.explanationZh: 正確答案為 C。根據文章第五段提到的「ripple effect」以及第六段提到「it will take time for the airlines to catch up and clear the backlog」，可以推論出飛機和機組人員因延誤而無法準時抵達下一站，導致後續連鎖反應。選項 A、B、D 皆未在文中提及，且不符合航空業運作的邏輯。

quiz.question: In the final paragraph, what does the word 'fragility' mean as it is used in the context of transportation infrastructure?

options.A: The tendency to be easily broken or disrupted.
options.B: The high cost of maintaining modern equipment.
options.C: The complexity of training air traffic controllers.
options.D: The physical weakness of airplane materials.

quiz.explanationZh: 正確答案為 A。文中提到「fragility of our transportation infrastructure」後，緊接著說明當電腦協調中斷時，數百萬人會受到影響，這顯示系統雖然先進但極易因單點故障而癱瘓。選項 B、C 雖是航空業的挑戰，但非 fragility 在此處的語意；選項 D 則是將詞彙誤解為物理上的脆弱，與基礎設施的系統性脆弱不符。

quiz.question: What is the primary message of this article?

options.A: The FAA is responsible for all financial losses caused by flight delays.
options.B: Modern air travel is unsafe due to outdated computer systems.
options.C: Aviation infrastructure is highly dependent on technology, making it vulnerable to system failures.
options.D: Passengers should avoid flying on Fridays to prevent being stuck in airports.

quiz.explanationZh: 正確答案為 C。文章從 FAA 的停飛事件切入，分析了現代航空對電腦系統的依賴（第四段），並在結尾總結了這種基礎設施的脆弱性（第七段），這正是全文的核心主旨。選項 A 非文章重點；選項 B 過度誇大，文中提到飛行通常很安全；選項 D 僅是針對特定事件的建議，非文章主旨。
